newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq to choose managing director today.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq to choose managing director today.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom's board of directors is due to meet this evening to choose a new managing director for the company, Bezeq's spokeswoman said on Monday.

Sources at the company said Yoram Turbowicz, who has resigned as head of the Industry and Trade Ministry's restrictive business practices division, will be chosen as Bezeq's next head. He replaces Yitzhak Kaul.
The spokeswoman would not comment on candidates for managing director or any other details about the appointment.
Turbowicz headed the division, which enforces anti-trust laws, for six years. He is due to leave next month.

The Bezeq appointment, regarded as one of the top management jobs in Israel, has been the subject of much press speculation in recent weeks. Among the other candidates rumoured to have been under consideration were Yehoshua Gleitman, industry ministry director-general, and Reuven Avi-Tal, managing director of Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.

Kaul, who has been named managing director of Clal Israel Ltd effective April 1, headed state-owned Bezeq for five years during which the company has been gradually shorn of key segments of its telecommunications monopoly.

The new managing director will be facing new competitive challenges for Bezeq in international calling sometime later this year, after licenses were awarded to two groups in November. By the end of 1998, the government has said it plans to open local and inter-urban phone service to competition, as well as telecommunications infrastructure.
In addition, the government is expected to make a global offering of Bezeq shares later this year.
